newsitem.title: USA: Senate calls for counsel probe of campaign funds.
newsitem.headline: Senate calls for counsel probe of campaign funds.

text.p: The Senate voted on party lines Wednesday to call on Attorney General Janet Reno to seek appointment of an independent counsel to investigate allegations of illegal campaign fund raising in the 1996 presidential campaign.

By a 55-44 vote, the Senate approved a non-binding resolution saying there had been "specific, credible information" of possible criminal violations by the Democratic National Commmitee and President Clinton's campaign.
Reno has ordered a preliminary investigation but has said no grounds have yet been found for applying for an independent counsel.

Democrats called the resolution, proposed by Majority Leader Trent Lott, blatantly political and proposed an alternative saying Reno should exercise her best judgment without regard to political pressures. It was killed by a 58-41 vote.
Republicans on the Senate and House judiciary committees have already petitioned Reno to begin procedures to ask a special three-judge panel to appoint an independent counsel.
In addition, committees in both the House and the Senate are conducting their own investigations into campaign finance irregularities.
